beats.label: S1 · Vampires walk into a bar
beats.text: Synthetic blood has let vampires go public. In small-town Bon Temps, telepathic waitress Sookie meets 173-year-old Bill Compton and finds she can't hear his thoughts.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the world's premise and the central pairing that drives the series.

beats.label: S1 · A serial killer targets fangbangers
beats.text: Local women who sleep with vampires start turning up strangled. Sookie's brother Jason is the first suspect, and the town's fear of vampires curdles into open hostility.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's spine — the murder mystery driving every subplot.

beats.label: S1 · Sookie and Bill, and Gran
beats.text: Sookie comes home to find her grandmother Adele murdered in the kitchen. In her grief, she goes to Bill and loses her virginity to him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Locks in the central romance and removes Sookie's anchor, isolating her.

beats.label: S1 · Fangtasia and Eric
beats.text: Chasing leads, Sookie is dragged into Shreveport's vampire bar Fangtasia and its thousand-year-old sheriff Eric Northman, who immediately marks her as useful.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Eric and the larger vampire hierarchy that will drive later seasons.

beats.label: S1 · Bill's punishment
beats.text: Bill kills another vampire to save Sookie and is sentenced by the vampire Magister to make a new one — a teenage girl named Jessica, whom he reluctantly turns.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Creates Jessica, a recurring character, and shows vampire law has teeth.

beats.label: S1 · Rene is the killer
beats.text: Sookie realises the killer is Arlene's fiancé Rene, actually a man named Drew Marshall who hunts fangbangers. She kills him with a shovel as a badly burned Bill crawls out of the ground to help.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves the season's mystery and cements Bill's devotion to Sookie.

beats.label: S1 · A body in the car
beats.text: Life seems to settle — until the Merlotte's staff help a drunk Detective Andy to his car and find a corpse in the back seat.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season-ending hook that launches S2's Maryann arc.

cliffhanger.text: The fangbanger killer is dead and Sookie and Bill are together, but a fresh corpse has just turned up in Andy Bellefleur's car outside Merlotte's — and Lafayette has been jumped and dragged off by someone unseen.
questions: Whose body is in Andy's car, and who put it there?
Who abducted Lafayette, and what do they want from him?
Now that Bon Temps knows vampires can love, what happens when something worse than a vampire arrives?

characters.name: Sookie Stackhouse
characters.line: Telepathic waitress at Merlotte's, now dating Bill; her grandmother's murder has left her and Jason as the last of the family.

characters.name: Bill Compton
characters.line: 173-year-old vampire, Sookie's boyfriend, and reluctant maker of a newly turned teenager named Jessica.

characters.name: Jason Stackhouse
characters.line: Sookie's brother — cleared of the murders, briefly hooked on vampire blood, and drifting toward the anti-vampire Fellowship of the Sun.

characters.name: Sam Merlotte
characters.line: Sookie's boss and secret shapeshifter; loves her, lost her to Bill, and has quietly revealed his nature to her.

characters.name: Tara Thornton
characters.line: Sookie's best friend, bartender at Merlotte's, freshly out of jail and taken in by a wealthy stranger named Maryann Forrester.

characters.name: Eric Northman
characters.line: Thousand-year-old Viking vampire and sheriff of Area 5, running Fangtasia in Shreveport and already interested in Sookie's abilities.

characters.name: Jessica Hamby
characters.line: The teenage girl Bill was forced to turn as punishment — new, impulsive, and now his responsibility.

characters.name: Lafayette Reynolds
characters.line: Merlotte's cook, small-time V dealer, Tara's cousin — attacked in the parking lot at season's end and missing.

beats.label: S2 · Maryann moves in
beats.text: The stranger who bailed Tara out, Maryann Forrester, installs herself in Sookie's orbit. Sam recognises her as the woman who raped him as a teenage runaway and lives in terror.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the season's antagonist and Sam's personal stake in stopping her.

beats.label: S2 · Dallas and the Fellowship
beats.text: Eric sends Sookie and Bill to Dallas to find a missing vampire elder, Godric. Sookie infiltrates the anti-vampire Fellowship of the Sun church and is taken hostage.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's second spine, introducing the vampire-vs-Fellowship politics.

beats.label: S2 · Jason inside the church
beats.text: Jason joins the Fellowship's Light of Day camp and sleeps with the pastor's wife Sarah Newlin. When he learns Sookie is a captive, he switches sides and helps break her out.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Jason on the Newlins' radar and plants Steve and Sarah as recurring enemies.

beats.label: S2 · Godric chooses the sun
beats.text: The rescued Godric — Eric's ancient maker — is stripped of his sheriff post and decides he is done. He walks into the sunrise on a Dallas rooftop as Sookie sits with him and Eric weeps.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Godric's death reshapes Eric emotionally and gives him a bond with Sookie that carries forward.

beats.label: S2 · Bon Temps loses its mind
beats.text: Back home, Maryann is revealed as a maenad — an immortal follower of Dionysus — putting the whole town in a black-eyed orgiastic trance and nesting an unhatched egg on Gran's bed.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Escalates the season's real threat while Sookie was in Dallas.

beats.label: S2 · Killing the god
beats.text: Sam offers himself as a sacrifice, shifts into a bull, and gores Maryann's heart out. Eggs, restored to himself, remembers he killed under her spell, holds Andy at knifepoint, and Jason shoots him dead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the maenad plot and leaves Jason carrying a killing he'll bury.

beats.label: S2 · A proposal and a disappearance
beats.text: Bill takes Sookie to a French restaurant and proposes. She steps into the bathroom to compose herself; when she comes back, the place is in disarray and Bill is gone.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The direct hook into S3 — the missing-Bill mystery that opens the next season.

cliffhanger.text: Sookie has just decided to marry Bill, and now Bill has been snatched out of a French restaurant. Sookie has no idea by whom, or why.
questions: Who abducted Bill Compton, and what do they want with him?
What actually is Sookie — Maryann sensed something not-human, and her hand glowed with light?
Now that Jason has killed Eggs, can he live with himself, and will anyone ever find out?

characters.name: Sookie Stackhouse
characters.line: Bill's fiancée for about ten minutes before he vanished; still doesn't know what she is, only that it isn't fully human.

characters.name: Bill Compton
characters.line: Missing, abducted from a restaurant parking lot after proposing to Sookie.

characters.name: Eric Northman
characters.line: Sheriff of Area 5, freshly grieving his maker Godric and increasingly fixated on Sookie.

characters.name: Jason Stackhouse
characters.line: Fresh off shooting a mind-controlled Eggs dead as he held Andy at knifepoint; the town believes it was justified, but Jason knows he pulled the trigger.

characters.name: Tara Thornton
characters.line: Emerging from Maryann's spell, grieving the boyfriend Jason just killed, and estranged from her mother.

characters.name: Sam Merlotte
characters.line: The shifter who killed Maryann; has begun searching for his biological parents.

characters.name: Jessica Hamby
characters.line: Baby vampire in a relationship with Hoyt Fortenberry, and has secretly fed on a trucker at a gas station.

characters.name: Steve and Sarah Newlin
characters.line: The Fellowship of the Sun's leaders, humiliated in Dallas — Steve's church is broken and Sarah wants Jason back.

characters.name: Lafayette Reynolds
characters.line: Traumatised after being caged and fed on at Fangtasia, working again at Merlotte's, and being pushed by Eric back into dealing V.

beats.label: S3 · Werewolves took Bill
beats.text: Sookie learns Bill was taken by werewolves working for Russell Edgington, the ancient Vampire King of Mississippi. Eric assigns her a werewolf bodyguard, Alcide Herveaux, to hunt him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Russell, werewolves, and Alcide — all central to the season and beyond.

beats.label: S3 · Bill switches sides
beats.text: In Russell's Jackson mansion Bill submits, telling Russell that Queen Sophie-Anne is broke and selling vampire blood. He even helps drain a stripper for his new king.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The apparent betrayal that fractures Bill and Sookie's relationship all season.

beats.label: S3 · Eric's thousand-year grudge
beats.text: Eric recognises a Viking crown in Russell's mansion as his father's — Russell slaughtered Eric's family a millennium ago. Everything Eric does from here is aimed at killing Russell.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reframes Eric's whole arc as personal vengeance, not politics.

beats.label: S3 · Sookie is part-faerie
beats.text: After Bill nearly drains her he tells her the truth: she is part faerie, which is why her blood is intoxicating and why every vampire wants her. Russell now knows too.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's central revelation about Sookie, load-bearing for every following season.

beats.label: S3 · Russell on the news
beats.text: Enraged by Eric's murder of his consort Talbot, Russell walks into a live TV broadcast, tears out a news anchor's spine, and declares war on humanity and the mainstreaming AVL.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Cements Russell as an existential threat and the season's iconic image.

beats.label: S3 · Buried in concrete
beats.text: Sookie's fae light lets Eric restrain Russell in sunlight. They chain him and encase him in a slab of concrete — alive, conscious, and buried in a parking garage.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Russell as an active threat while leaving him alive for later.

beats.label: S3 · Sookie learns Bill was sent
beats.text: Eric tells Sookie that Bill was originally dispatched by Queen Sophie-Anne to procure her, and let the Rattrays nearly kill her so she'd take his blood. Sookie throws them both out and, at Gran's grave, follows Claudine into the fae world.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the Bill-Sookie relationship in betrayal and sets up her disappearance.

cliffhanger.text: Russell is buried alive in concrete, Bill has invited Queen Sophie-Anne over for a duel to the death, and Sookie has just walked into the faerie world with Claudine.
questions: How long will Russell stay in that concrete grave, and who will let him out?
What is the faerie world actually like, and how long is Sookie going to be gone?
Bill was sent to procure Sookie for a queen — is anything he's ever said to her real?

characters.name: Sookie Stackhouse
characters.line: Part-faerie, freshly aware she was set up by Bill from day one, and just walked out of this world with her cousin Claudine.

characters.name: Bill Compton
characters.line: Exposed as Sophie-Anne's plant, banished by Sookie, and about to duel his queen to the death over what he knows about Sookie's heritage.

characters.name: Eric Northman
characters.line: Avenged his family on Russell after a thousand years, betrayed Bill by locking him up too, and is now the vampire Sookie last shouted at.

characters.name: Russell Edgington
characters.line: 3000-year-old vampire King of Mississippi, encased alive in concrete under a parking garage after publicly declaring war on humanity.

characters.name: Alcide Herveaux
characters.line: Werewolf bodyguard who fought Russell's pack alongside Sookie; broke with his fiancée Debbie Pelt after she turned on them.

characters.name: Jason Stackhouse
characters.line: New Bon Temps deputy, now the reluctant guardian of Hotshot's leaderless were-panther community after Crystal was taken by Felton.

characters.name: Sam Merlotte
characters.line: Reeling from meeting his biological family — his brother Tommy robbed him and vanished.

characters.name: Tara Thornton
characters.line: Learned Sam is a shifter and that her mother is sleeping with a preacher, and has left Bon Temps.

characters.name: Jessica and Hoyt
characters.line: Engaged over Maxine Fortenberry's furious objections; Maxine has quietly bought an anti-vampire rifle.

characters.name: Lafayette Reynolds
characters.line: Dating Jesús, whom he has just discovered is a brujo — a male witch.

beats.label: S4 · A year is gone
beats.text: Sookie escapes the faerie realm to find twelve months have passed. Bill is now King of Louisiana — he deposed and executed Sophie-Anne on the AVL's orders.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resets every character's position; Bill's throne matters through the rest of the series.

beats.label: S4 · A witch curses Eric
beats.text: Local Wiccan Marnie is possessed by the vengeful 17th-century witch Antonia and strips Eric of his memory. Sookie hides the childlike amnesiac at her house.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the season's antagonist and the romance that reshuffles Sookie's love triangle.

beats.label: S4 · Sookie and Eric
beats.text: With his cruelty gone, Sookie falls for the amnesiac Eric and they finally sleep together. When Sookie breaks Marnie's spell his memory returns and both his selves know they love her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Permanently changes the Bill-Sookie-Eric triangle going into every subsequent season.

beats.label: S4 · Antonia burns the sun into vampires
beats.text: Antonia casts spells forcing vampires into daylight. Bill's counter-attack ends in a public bloodbath at a tolerance festival, wrecking mainstreaming and Bill's political cover.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's public catastrophe that hardens human-vampire relations.

beats.label: S4 · Killing the witch
beats.text: At the Moon Goddess Emporium, Jesús and Lafayette harness a sacrifice to sever Marnie from Antonia. Bill and Eric storm in and kill Marnie.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the witch war and hands off the season's tail to Marnie-in-Lafayette.

beats.label: S4 · Debbie kills Tara
beats.text: A jealous, strung-out Debbie Pelt breaks into Sookie's house with a shotgun. Tara shoves Sookie clear and takes the blast to the head; Sookie kills Debbie with the same gun.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season-ending shock that S5 opens on.

beats.label: S4 · Russell walks
beats.text: Elsewhere, Nan Flanagan is executed by Bill after she confesses she's plotting against the Authority — and Alcide discovers Russell's concrete grave has been dug open and emptied.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Russell and the Authority conflict back on the board for S5.

cliffhanger.text: Tara is bleeding out on Sookie's kitchen floor from a shotgun blast meant for Sookie. Bill has just killed the AVL's spokeswoman, and somewhere out there Russell Edgington is loose again.
questions: Can Tara possibly be saved, and if so, at what cost?
Who dug Russell out of the concrete, and what will he do first?
Marnie's spirit slipped into Lafayette — is she still riding him?

characters.name: Sookie Stackhouse
characters.line: Just killed Debbie Pelt in self-defence, cradling the dying Tara, and in love with both Bill and Eric but chose to be alone.

characters.name: Bill Compton
characters.line: King of Louisiana, having dealt Nan Flanagan the True Death to keep Sookie's fae heritage secret from the Authority.

characters.name: Eric Northman
characters.line: Restored to his old self but now genuinely in love with Sookie; still loyal to Pam, who is jealous of Sookie.

characters.name: Jason Stackhouse
characters.line: Sleeping with Jessica; Hoyt has broken with them both after Jason confessed.

characters.name: Tara Thornton
characters.line: Just took a shotgun blast to the head saving Sookie.

characters.name: Jessica Hamby
characters.line: Broke up with Hoyt to be with Jason on her own terms — sex only, no relationship.

characters.name: Pam Swynford De Beaufort
characters.line: Eric's progeny, cured of Marnie's decay curse but still resentful of Sookie's hold on him.

characters.name: Alcide Herveaux
characters.line: Broke with Debbie after she went bad, discovered Russell's empty concrete grave, and doesn't yet know Sookie killed Debbie.

characters.name: Lafayette Reynolds
characters.line: Grieving Jesús, who was killed by possessed-Lafayette after severing Marnie from Antonia — and possessed at season's end by Marnie's spirit.

characters.name: Steve Newlin
characters.line: Presumed dead for a season, has just turned up on Jason's doorstep as a newly minted vampire.

beats.label: S5 · Turning Tara
beats.text: To save Tara, Sookie and Lafayette let Pam turn her into a vampire. Tara wakes up furious at both of them and estranged from her mother all over again.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Keeps Tara in play as a vampire, and binds her to Pam as her maker.

beats.label: S5 · The Authority takes Bill and Eric
beats.text: The Vampire Authority arrests Bill and Eric for killing Nan Flanagan. Eric's long-lost 'sister' Nora rescues them, but they are recaptured and dragged before Guardian Roman in New Orleans.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Moves the season into the Authority — the central power structure of S5.

beats.label: S5 · Hunt Russell to earn a pardon
beats.text: Roman spares Bill and Eric on condition they hunt down the escaped Russell Edgington. They find him weak in a hospital feeding on humans and drag him back to the Authority.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's mission plot that pulls Bill and Eric inside the Authority.

beats.label: S5 · Russell kills Roman
beats.text: At his own execution Russell breaks free and drives a stake through Guardian Roman's chest. Chancellor Salome reveals she freed him — the Authority's fundamentalist Sanguinistas now run the building.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Power flip inside the Authority; every subsequent beat comes from this.

beats.label: S5 · Sookie is fae royalty
beats.text: Sookie and Jason learn their parents were killed because of Sookie's fae blood, and that centuries ago a Stackhouse ancestor signed a contract promising a fae-bearing heir to a vampire named Warlow.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the Warlow contract that drives S6, and reframes the parents' death.

beats.label: S5 · Drinking Lilith
beats.text: The Chancellors drink the blood of the vampire progenitor Lilith and go feral, killing at a wedding. Godric's ghost tells Eric to save Nora and stop them.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Turns Bill's arc dark and gives Eric a mission that splits them.

beats.label: S5 · Billith
beats.text: Sookie, Eric, Jason, Tara, Nora, Pam and Jessica raid the Authority. Bill tricks Salome into drinking silver-laced blood, then drinks the last of Lilith's; his body dissolves and reforms as a bloody, god-like vampire.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's final image and the direct setup for S6.

cliffhanger.text: Bill has drunk Lilith's blood, exploded in a pool of gore, and re-formed as something monstrous. Eric is screaming at Sookie to run.
questions: What has Bill become, and is any of him still in there?
The Authority is dead — who fills the vacuum, and what happens to the mainstreaming truce?
With Warlow's contract still valid, when does he come to collect Sookie?

characters.name: Sookie Stackhouse
characters.line: Just watched Bill transform into a monster after helping his friends kill the Authority.

characters.name: Bill Compton
characters.line: No longer Bill — reborn as a Lilith-figure in a pool of blood.

characters.name: Eric Northman
characters.line: Sobered by Godric's ghost, turned against Lilith's cult, and terrified of what Bill has become.

characters.name: Jason Stackhouse
characters.line: Learned vampires murdered his parents and has emerged from the Authority raid violently anti-vampire.

characters.name: Tara Thornton
characters.line: Now a vampire, Pam's progeny, tending bar at Fangtasia and sharing a passionate kiss with Pam.

characters.name: Pam Swynford De Beaufort
characters.line: Officially released by Eric so she can survive without him; Tara's maker.

characters.name: Jessica Hamby
characters.line: Sided with Bill inside the Authority but joined the raid to bring him down.

characters.name: Sam Merlotte
characters.line: Killed a Chancellor from inside her body to help rescue Emma; the shifter-child now returned to her wolf grandmother.

characters.name: Alcide Herveaux
characters.line: Killed pack leader J.D. and taken over the Shreveport pack, promising a return to pack basics.

characters.name: Nora Gainesborough
characters.line: Eric's fellow progeny of Godric, ex-Authority insider now on the run with him.

beats.label: S6 · Governor Burrell's war
beats.text: Louisiana Governor Truman Burrell declares open war on vampires, criminalising Tru Blood production and opening a secret research camp where captured vampires are experimented on.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's political through-line that drives the camp arc.

beats.label: S6 · Warlow arrives
beats.text: The vampire promised Sookie two centuries ago — Warlow — crosses into Bon Temps. He turns out to be Ben, a charming fae-vampire hybrid who saves Jason and courts Sookie.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Personifies the contract Sookie inherited last season.

beats.label: S6 · Lilith orders Bill to save them all
beats.text: Bill's Lilith visions show every vampire he knows burning in sunlight. He becomes obsessed with using Warlow's blood to make his kind daywalkers.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains Bill's whole season and connects him to Warlow.

beats.label: S6 · Vamp Camp
beats.text: Eric, Pam, Tara, Jessica, Nora and Willa end up inside Burrell's camp. Sarah Newlin, now the governor's zealot, contaminates the state's Tru Blood supply with hepatitis V to wipe vampires out.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts the whole cast in one place and introduces the Hep-V plague.

beats.label: S6 · Nora dies of Hep-V
beats.text: Nora is infected in the camp and dies in Eric's arms. Bill refuses to intervene, breaking the last of Eric's loyalty to him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Motivates Eric's rage-fuelled rescue and drives a wedge between him and Bill.

beats.label: S6 · The camp burns
beats.text: Powered by Warlow's blood, Bill daywalks into Vamp Camp and offers himself as a shield so the trapped vampires can escape into the sun. Eric kills Steve Newlin; Sarah escapes.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves the camp plot and cements Bill's messiah complex.

beats.label: S6 · Warlow dies, six months later
beats.text: Jason stakes Warlow with Niall's help; the daywalking gift dies with him and, in Sweden, Eric ignites in the sun. Six months on, Bon Temps holds a 'pair with a healthy vampire' meet — and a horde of Hep-V infected vampires closes in.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the exact premise of the final season.

cliffhanger.text: Hepatitis V has spread nationwide and turned infected vampires into feral killers. As Bon Temps hosts its first vampire-pairing meeting at Bellefleur's, a horde of infected vampires descends on the party.
questions: Did Eric really just die naked and burning on a Swedish mountaintop?
Can Bon Temps' human-vampire pairings survive a full-on Hep-V attack?
With Warlow gone and Sarah Newlin loose, who has the cure — or knows there is one?

characters.name: Sookie Stackhouse
characters.line: Back with Alcide, no longer promised to any vampire; Warlow is dead by her brother's hand.

characters.name: Bill Compton
characters.line: Human-powers gone with Warlow's death, now writing a book about his ordeal and preaching human-vampire cooperation.

characters.name: Eric Northman
characters.line: Last seen bursting into flames on a snowy Swedish mountainside — fate unclear.

characters.name: Jason Stackhouse
characters.line: In a possessive relationship with the ancient vampire Violet Mazurski, who saved his life inside the camp.

characters.name: Jessica Hamby
characters.line: Newly bonded with fellow ex-inmate James; still atoning for killing three of Andy Bellefleur's fae daughters.

characters.name: Sam Merlotte
characters.line: The new mayor of Bon Temps, with a pregnant Nicole.

characters.name: Tara Thornton
characters.line: Reconciling with her born-again mother Lettie Mae, who has offered to feed her.

characters.name: Pam Swynford De Beaufort
characters.line: Freed from the camp, and still Tara's maker.

characters.name: Sarah Newlin
characters.line: On the run after tainting the state's Tru Blood supply.

characters.name: Andy Bellefleur
characters.line: Sheriff and single father raising his surviving fae daughter Adilyn, engaged to Holly.

beats.label: S7 · The raid on Bellefleur's
beats.text: Hep-V vampires storm the mixer, killing several townspeople and dragging Arlene, Holly and Nicole off to Fangtasia. In the chaos Tara is killed, leaving Lettie Mae hallucinating her ghost.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's inciting event and Tara's exit.

beats.label: S7 · Eric is alive, and dying
beats.text: In Morocco and then France, Pam finally finds Eric. He is Hep-V positive, world-weary and ready to die, until Pam tells him Sarah Newlin is still out there.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Confirms Eric survived and gives him a target for the season.

beats.label: S7 · Alcide dies, Bill is infected
beats.text: The rescue of Arlene and Holly ends in a shootout: Alcide is killed. Bill later discovers he too is Hep-V positive — infected by drinking from Sookie, who unknowingly carried the virus.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Alcide and turns Bill's death into the season's emotional spine.

beats.label: S7 · Sarah is the cure
beats.text: Eric and Pam hunt Sarah with the Japanese Yakonomo corporation. When Eric drinks from her his Hep-V is instantly cured — she took her own antidote and is now a living vaccine.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's central discovery that reshuffles every vampire's fate.

beats.label: S7 · Bill refuses the cure
beats.text: Offered Sarah's blood, Bill turns it down. He asks Jessica to release him and begs Sookie to end him, believing his death will free her to have a normal human life.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the finale and closes the Sookie–Bill relationship on Bill's terms.

beats.label: S7 · The grave
beats.text: Bill gives Jessica away in a hurried wedding to Hoyt, wills his land to Andy on the condition they live there, and lies in his Civil War grave. Sookie helps him drive a stake through his own chest and fills the grave in.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The show's central death and Sookie's release.

beats.label: S7 · Four years later
beats.text: Eric and Pam run New Blood — the synthetic cure marketed worldwide — while secretly keeping Sarah locked in Fangtasia's basement to feed on. Sookie hosts Thanksgiving in Bon Temps, married and pregnant, with Jason, Sam and their families around the table.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The series' final resting position for every survivor.

cliffhanger.text: There is no cliffhanger — this is the series finale. Bill is dead in his Civil War grave; Sookie has a husband and a child on the way; Eric and Pam are billionaires; Sarah Newlin sits chained in the Fangtasia basement, milked forever.
questions: Did Sookie make the right call letting Bill die instead of forcing the cure on him?
How long can Eric and Pam keep Sarah alive down there?
Is 'normal' actually what Sookie ever wanted?

characters.name: Sookie Stackhouse
characters.line: Ended the show married to an unnamed man, expecting a child, hosting Thanksgiving in Bon Temps — with Bill dead by her hand.

characters.name: Bill Compton
characters.line: Refused the Hep-V cure and chose to be staked in his own grave by Sookie.

characters.name: Eric Northman
characters.line: Cured by Sarah's blood, running the multi-billion-dollar New Blood corporation with Pam.

characters.name: Pam Swynford De Beaufort
characters.line: Eric's business partner in New Blood, quietly monetising a captive Sarah Newlin as a private feed.

characters.name: Jason Stackhouse
characters.line: Married to Hoyt's ex Brigette, three kids, still Sookie's brother and closest ally.

characters.name: Jessica Hamby
characters.line: Married Hoyt in Bill's final act; released as Bill's progeny and living in his old house.

characters.name: Sam Merlotte
characters.line: Left Bon Temps with Nicole and their baby daughter, but returned for Sookie's Thanksgiving.

characters.name: Sarah Newlin
characters.line: Imprisoned in Fangtasia's basement as a living Hep-V cure, haunted by the ghost of Steve Newlin.
